title: SLO budgeting + privacy-aware observability (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight sketch for combining SLO budgeting with privacy-aware telemetry for inference services. This doc is intentionally informal — goal is to capture ideas and tradeoffs before we formalize metric contracts.

Background / why now:
- Observability costs are increasing (cardinality explosion + retention).
- We need a defensible SLO budgeting method for hosted and dedicated tiers (predictable spend + clear signal for alerts).
- Privacy/regulatory requests (GDPR/C7X) push us to reduce raw payload retention and avoid PII in traces while keeping debuggability for production incidents.

High-level goals:
- Define a small set of canonical metrics for inference quality, performance, and cost that map directly to SLIs.
- Propose sampling & aggregation rules that limit PII exposure and cardinality growth.
- Sketch dashboard wireframes and ownership for SLO + incident triage.
- Produce a migration checklist for current dashboards that use raw prompts / full user ids.

SLO budgeting approach (sketch):
1) Tiered SLOs per offering: hosted-api (developer, best-effort cost), dedicated (enterprise, committed throughput), private (customer-managed).
2) Budget unit = "SLO tokens" — convert token-level SLOs to monthly budget using observed per-token cost. This ties observability sensitivity to dollars.
3) Error SLOs: p99 server-side latency, user-experienced tail latency (including network), and correctness (model/regression) for critical prompt sets.
4) Burn rate policy: automated increases in telemetry (higher sample rate) when burn rate > threshold for the budget window, and automatic throttling of non-essential traces when budget exhausted.

Metric definitions (canonical, short names + description):
- inference.request.count: count of inference requests accepted by routing layer (label: route, model_variant, region, tenant_type).
- inference.token.count: total input+output tokens processed (label: model_variant, seq_length_bucket).
- inference.p99.server_latency_ms: p99 latency from request enter to final token emitted (exclude client-side network).
- inference.p99.user_latency_ms: p99 latency including proxy/client network hop (synthesized where possible).
- kv_cache.hit_rate: fraction of requests served from KV/prefix caches (label: model_variant, tenant).
- batching.efficiency_ratio: mean(batch_size) / max_possible_batch_size (helps quantify batching headroom).
- model.fallback.rate: rate at which requests fallback to lower-capacity model (labels: fallback_reason).
- error.ingestion.rate: rate of infra-level errors (OOM, kernel-failure, grpc-timeout).
- cost.per_1000_tokens_usd: derived metric mapping token usage to $ (billing rate).
- trace.sampled.count: count of traced requests after sampling policy applied (to monitor sampling coverage).

Metric labeling guidance:
- Keep tenant id hashed (sha256:8) rather than raw user id when retention of identity is unnecessary.
- Avoid storing full prompts in labels or metrics. Use prompt-set ids or fingerprinting for blackbox testing.
- Limit high-cardinality labels (e.g., model_commit_hash) to lower-frequency rollup metrics only.

Tracing notes (context propagation & privacy):
- Propagate trace context via header: Redwood-Trace and standard W3C traceparent. Fall back to router-assigned trace id.
- Span naming convention: <component>.<operation> — examples: router.resolve, runtime.batch.exec, kvcache.lookup, runtime.generate_token.
- Trace anchors: on long-running spans (runtime.generate_token) emit sparse span events with token-range offsets, not raw tokens.
- Redaction: any span annotation derived from prompt text must be hashed or redacted. Use prompt-set id tag instead.
- Sampling: base rate 0.5% across production; automatic upsampling for anomalous requests — define anomaly triggers (latency > p99 * 1.5 OR 5xx).
- Debug mode: when a customer enables deep-debug (enterprise only), capture full trace and prompt for a fixed retention TTL and explicit consent flow.

Dashboard notes (sketch widgets and layout):
Top row (SLO health + burn):
- SLO overview bar: %SLO met (30d), current burn-rate meter, budget remaining (tokens -> $).
- p99 latency sparkline vs SLO threshold.

Middle row (triage + routing):
- Per-route latency heatmap (rows: routes, cols: latency buckets).
- Fallback rate stacked area chart (reasons).
- KV cache hit rate trend + top tenants with low hit-rate (hashed ids).

Bottom row (cost + sampling):
- cost.per_1000_tokens_usd trend and weekly forecast.
- trace sampled coverage map: fraction of requests traced by route/region.
- anomalous event list (auto-populated from alert engine).

Dashboard ownership & runbook pointers:
- Owner: eng-observability (primary: Evelyn Shaw; backup: Diego Morales).
- Oncall playbook link: referenced in linked_artifacts.
- Escalation: if p99 latency > SLO for 3 consecutive 5m windows, page SRE. If burn-rate > 0.7, page Observability-Eng.

Privacy and retention constraints (rules):
- Default retention for sampled traces: 7 days. Enterprise opt-in for 30/90 days with contract.
- Traces with prompt-set id only; full prompt kept only for debug-mode with explicit consent.
- Aggregation windows: use 1m raw aggregation for 48h then 5m rollups thereafter to control storage.
- PII filters: any free-text fields are run through PII detector; if positive, replace with token <REDACTED>.

Operational tradeoffs noted:
- Lower sampling reduces cost but degrades triage signal for infrequent but high-impact failures.
- Hashing tenant ids limits targeted debugging for customer support; propose a reversible-hash escrow for enterprise with strict access controls.
- SLO budget enforcement needs cross-team buy-in (billing, product, infra) to be actionable.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is the canonical "token" definition across models (input+output vs model-specific counters)?
- Precise burn-rate thresholds for staging vs prod vs dedicated customers.
- Policy for temporary full-trace capture during incidents (who can enable, approval flow).
- Retention for metrics used for billing disputes (need 1 year?).

Next steps / proposed milestones:
- (1 week) Finalize metric name list and labels -> establish metric contracts (owners assigned).
- (2 weeks) Implement sampling policy prototype in router; add trace-sampling telemetry metric.
- (3 weeks) Dashboard wireframe + handoff to data viz (small iteration with screenshots).
- (4–6 weeks) Pilot on one hosted tenant and one dedicated pool, collect burn-rate data and tune.

Notes / references:
- See linked Jira (OBS-342) for earlier SLO budgeting threads.
- This doc intentionally omits exact SLO values — will propose concrete numbers after 2-week pilot.

— Evelyn
